unit.title: Clinical Office Practice and Patient Safety

sections.learningObjectives:
- Maintain a safe patient room and office environment by identifying and correcting common fall and trip hazards.
- Perform environmental cleaning and disinfection correctly, including high-touch surfaces, contact times, and spill cleanup.
- Store and dispose of sharps and chemicals safely, following labeling, SDS, and bloodborne-pathogen precautions.
- Recognize hazards and escalate them through proper channels when they cannot be safely handled by the assistant.
sections.eli10:
### Question 1

Imagine a path full of toys on the floor; it is easy to trip over them. Keeping walkways clear is the same idea, so no one trips.

### Question 2

If you spill water on the kitchen floor, you stay close and warn people while someone gets a towel and a sign, so nobody slips.

### Question 3

It is like putting up a 'caution' sign before people reach a slippery spot so they can walk around it safely.

### Question 4

Like tucking a charger cable along the wall instead of across the floor, so no one catches their foot on it.

### Question 5

Keep the thing someone leans on right next to them and the way clear, like leaving crutches by the chair so they can grab them easily.

### Question 6

It is like putting the brake on a rolling chair before standing up, so it does not slide out from under you.

### Question 7

Some floors are like a water slide when wet, while others are grippy like a doormat. The shiny ones are the slipperiest.

### Question 8

It is like a rug corner that flips up and catches your toe; the fix is to make it flat again or take it away.

### Question 9

If someone feels wobbly like they might tip over, you help them sit down first and go get an adult to help.

### Question 10

Like tidying up your room right after playing so it is ready and safe for the next time.

### Question 11

When a room is bright you can see where your feet are going, like a nightlight so you do not trip in the dark.

### Question 12

Everything has a home, like putting toys in the toy box instead of leaving them on the floor.

### Question 13

Do not leave a pile in the doorway for someone to trip over; carry it to where it belongs right away.

### Question 14

It is like a sturdy handle on a backpack that a helper holds to keep you steady while you walk.

### Question 15

Clean the floor like you dry a spill at home: use just enough water, warn people, and dry it so no one slips.

### Question 16

Tuck a dangling strap out of the way, like moving a backpack off the floor so no one trips.

### Question 17

A cord across the floor is like a tripwire; flat mats, rails, and signs are there to keep you safe.

### Question 18

It is like a bell you ring to call for help instead of trying to do something risky on your own.

### Question 19

Keep the bed low like a low step, and keep the help-bell and their things close so they do not have to get up alone.

### Question 20

Shoes with grippy bottoms are like tires with good tread; they help you not slide on a slippery floor.

### Question 21

Walk beside someone like you would hold the door and match their speed, so they feel safe and have a clear path.

### Question 22

A slip happens when your feet slide, like stepping on a wet spot in socks.

### Question 23

It is like standing a heavy water jug in a holder so it cannot fall over on someone's foot.

### Question 24

Oxygen is like wind on a campfire: it does not burn by itself but makes everything else burn much faster.

### Question 25

A trip is when your toe catches on something in the way, like a shoe left in the middle of the floor.

### Question 26

Rugs should lie flat and stay put, like a bath mat that does not slide around.

### Question 27

You keep the doorways clear like a fire drill path, so everyone can get out fast if there is danger.

### Question 28

Stay close to someone who might fall, like holding hands with a little kid near a busy road.

### Question 29

Lock the wheels like setting the brake on a stroller before you pick up the baby.

### Question 30

A good room is like a tidy, dry, and ready play area where nothing is in the way and everything is put away.

### Question 31

Cleaning is like washing dirt off a plate; it removes the mess you can see.

### Question 32

Washing removes dirt; disinfecting is the extra step that gets rid of the invisible germs too.

### Question 33

Things everyone touches, like door handles, need cleaning the most, just like you wipe the table where everyone eats.

### Question 34

It is like a timer on medicine: the cleaner has to sit on the surface for a certain time to work.

### Question 35

Reading the label is like reading instructions before using a strong cleaner, so you know to wear gloves and keep it away from your eyes.

### Question 36

Wipe like you clean a chalkboard from top to bottom, and do the clean spots before the messy ones.

### Question 37

It is like leaving soap on your hands for the full scrubbing time before you rinse, or it does not work.

### Question 38

Like using a fresh paper towel for each messy spot instead of wiping everything with one dirty rag.

### Question 39

Change the paper and wipe the table between people, like putting out a clean placemat for the next person.

### Question 40

Blood needs careful cleanup with gloves and special cleaner, like handling something messy and germy with protection.

### Question 41

Wear gloves like you would when touching something dirty or germy, to keep germs off your skin.

### Question 42

Make the cleaner fresh each time and never mix it with other cleaners, like not mixing two strong ingredients that react badly.

### Question 43

It is like two ingredients that should never be mixed because together they make a dangerous gas you should not breathe.

### Question 44

Throw regular trash in the trash can and save the special sharp box only for needles.

### Question 45

Carry the dirty laundry in a bag and wear gloves, and do not shake it around the room.

### Question 46

Wash your hands after taking off gloves, like washing up after messy work even if you wore gloves.

### Question 47

Refill it the right way, like refilling a soap bottle with the same soap, not watering it down.

### Question 48

Wash before and after cleaning, like cleaning your hands before and after handling food.

### Question 49

Wash the surface first, then use the germ-killer, like wiping food off a counter before spraying the cleaner.

### Question 50

Do not use expired cleaner, just like you do not take expired medicine; get a fresh one instead.

### Question 51

Keep cleaners in their own labeled bottles and far from food, like storing soap away from snacks.

### Question 52

Things everyone touches, like the classroom door handle, get wiped a lot because lots of hands touch them.

### Question 53

Use a clean wipe for each spot, like a fresh tissue for each sneeze, so you do not spread the mess around.

### Question 54

Suit up, soak it up, clean it, then kill the germs, and throw the mess away the right way.

### Question 55

Clean from high to low, like sweeping crumbs off the table down to the floor and sweeping the floor last.

### Question 56

It is a special hard box with a lid that needles go into so they cannot poke anyone.

### Question 57

Put the needle straight into the sharp box right where you used it, without carrying it around.

### Question 58

Keep your other hand far away and use a tool or one-hand trick, so the sharp tip never points at your fingers.

### Question 59

Never put your hand into the needle box; there are sharp, germy points inside.

### Question 60

Use a tool or ask a trained helper to pick up a stray needle, never your bare hands.

### Question 61

Treat broken glass like a needle: wear gloves and put it in a hard box, never your hands or the trash.

### Question 62

The needle box is hard, sealed, and labeled, with a lid that stays shut.

### Question 63

Put the needle box right where it is used, standing up, where little kids cannot reach it.

### Question 64

When the needle box is full, close it up and get a new one; never squish needles down or dump them out.

### Question 65

Only things that can poke or cut, like needles, go in the special sharp box.

### Question 66

Anything sharp that can break the skin and get germs on it belongs in the hard box.

### Question 67

Carry the needle box by its handle, standing up and closed, like carrying a full cup carefully.

### Question 68

The rule is: do not recap, and if you must, keep your other hand out of the way.

### Question 69

Every cleaner bottle must be labeled so people know what is inside, like a name tag on a lunchbox.

### Question 70

The SDS is like an instruction and safety card that tells you what to do if a chemical spills or gets on you.

### Question 71

Do not put cleaners up high, next to food, or in bottles with no label.

### Question 72

Keep things that can catch fire far from anything hot or flaming, like keeping spray cans away from the stove.

### Question 73

If you pour it into a new bottle, write what it is on the new bottle, just like labeling leftovers.

### Question 74

Never use, smell, or dump a mystery liquid; treat it as dangerous and tell a grown-up in charge.

### Question 75

If you cannot safely fix a problem, tell the person in charge, like telling a teacher about a broken step.

### Question 76

A broken cord is like a cracked wire; unplug it and tell someone so it gets fixed before anyone uses it.

### Question 77

For a big or mystery spill, get people away and call for the person in charge, like a fire drill for spills.

### Question 78

Say thank you, keep people away from the wobbly rail, and tell the person who fixes things.

### Question 79

Write down what happened right away, like telling a teacher about a spill as soon as it happens.

### Question 80

If someone falls, stay with them and get help, and do not move them until someone trained says it is safe.

### Question 81

Some problems you fix yourself; dangerous ones like broken needle boxes or chemical leaks you report.

### Question 82

When you are not sure, check the instructions and ask the person in charge instead of guessing.

### Question 83

A spill kit is a ready box of gloves and absorbent pads for cleaning up messes safely.

### Question 84

Warn people, tell the person in charge, and make sure it gets cleaned up, like flagging a broken stair and getting it fixed.
